slides.title: What is Machine Learning?
slides.subtitle: The Core Idea of Learning from Data
content: Machine Learning (ML) is a subset of Artificial Intelligence that enables systems to learn from data without being explicitly programmed.
Focuses on developing algorithms that can identify patterns, make predictions, and improve performance through experience.
Core idea: The more data an algorithm processes, the better it becomes at tasks like classification, prediction, and decision-making.
Unlike traditional programming, ML systems adapt and evolve as they encounter new data.
slides.notes: Machine Learning is all about learning from data. Instead of writing explicit rules, we train algorithms on examples. For instance, instead of coding rules to recognize cats, we show thousands of cat images to the algorithm, and it learns the patterns on its own.

slides.title: Types of Machine Learning
slides.subtitle: How Machines Learn Differently
content: Supervised Learning: Algorithms learn from labeled data (e.g., spam detection, house price prediction). The model is trained on input-output pairs.
Unsupervised Learning: Algorithms find hidden patterns in unlabeled data (e.g., customer segmentation, anomaly detection). No predefined answers are provided.
Reinforcement Learning: Agents learn through trial and error by receiving rewards or penalties (e.g., game AI, robotics). The goal is to maximize cumulative rewards.
slides.notes: There are three main types of Machine Learning. Supervised learning is like learning with a teacher, unsupervised learning is like exploring on your own, and reinforcement learning is like learning through feedback. Each type has unique strengths and use cases.

slides.title: Applications and Algorithms
slides.subtitle: Real-World Uses and Key Methods
content: Applications: ML powers healthcare diagnostics (e.g., disease detection), recommendation systems (e.g., Netflix), fraud detection (e.g., credit card monitoring), and self-driving cars.

Basic Algorithms: Linear Regression predicts continuous values, Decision Trees make decisions based on data splits, K-Means Clustering groups similar data points, and Neural Networks model complex patterns.
slides.notes: Machine Learning is everywhere! From Netflix suggesting shows to doctors diagnosing diseases, ML algorithms are transforming industries. Let's explore some fundamental algorithms that power these applications.

slides.title: Challenges and Ethical Considerations
slides.subtitle: Navigating the Complexities of ML
content: Challenges: Data quality issues (garbage in, garbage out), overfitting (models memorizing noise instead of patterns), and high computational costs.
Ethical Issues: Bias in data (e.g., discriminatory hiring algorithms), privacy concerns (e.g., data misuse), and job displacement due to automation.
Future: Responsible AI development emphasizes transparency, fairness, and accountability to ensure ML benefits society equitably.
slides.notes: While ML offers immense potential, it also poses significant challenges. Data bias can perpetuate discrimination, and privacy risks are growing. As future practitioners, we must prioritize ethical considerations to build trustworthy and inclusive AI systems.
